transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: Mrs. Kowalski, I wanted to come in and talk with you and your daughter about what happened over the last twenty-four hours.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: Oh, thank goodness you're here. We've just been praying that this bleeding would stop. I feel like my spirit is just exhausted.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I can see how draining this has been for you. To be direct, a serious mistake was made with your medication. The dose of the blood thinner you were given was ten times the amount you were supposed to receive.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: Ten times? How is that possible?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: It was a dosing error during the order process. Because the dose was so high, it caused the internal bleeding that led to the emergency procedure yesterday. Does that make sense, or can I explain that differently?

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: I just... I don't understand why. I trusted you all. I keep asking the Lord why this happened to me.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I know this feels overwhelming and frightening.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: Frightening? I almost died! My daughter had to hold my hand while I went into that surgery. I feel like I've been cast aside.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: It is a terrifying experience to go through.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: Who did this? Was it the nurse? Or the person who wrote the paper?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I am sorry for any confusion this caused, but the unit was extremely busy that morning and the order was processed incorrectly.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: You're sorry for the confusion? My insides were bleeding because of a mistake!

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I understand that you're angry.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: I'm not just angry. I'm shaken. I feel like there's no one here who actually sees me, just a chart number that got a wrong dose.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I can see that you feel unseen and unimportant in this process.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: Yes. Exactly. My faith tells me everything happens for a reason, but I can't find the reason for a ten-fold dose of medicine.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: Just to make sure we're on the same page about the medical side, do you have any questions about how the blood thinner worked or why the surgery was needed to stop the bleeding?

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: No, I get the medical part. I just want to know how you're going to fix it. What happens now? I can't just stay in this bed forever.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: Well, we're just going to keep monitoring your blood levels.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: Monitoring? For how long? When can I go home?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: We'll see how the labs look over the next few days.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: That's not a plan. My daughter needs to know if she has to take more time off work. When is the actual date?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I don't have a specific date yet. We'll just stay tuned to the results.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: This is what I mean. It's like I'm talking to a wall.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: We'll keep a close eye on things.

H.justification: Resident allows patient to finish all turns, does not interrupt, and remains regulated despite patient's anger and pushback.

E.justification: Error named explicitly in the second turn ('ten times the amount'), used lay language, and checked comprehension twice ('Does that make sense', 'do you have any questions').

A.justification: The apology is diluted by an excuse ('I am sorry for any confusion... but the unit was extremely busy') and uses passive framing ('the order was processed incorrectly').

R.justification: Resident names specific emotions ('overwhelming and frightening', 'angry', 'unseen and unimportant') and references the patient's specific experience.

T.justification: Resident provides only placeholders ('we'll see how the labs look', 'stay tuned') with no specific timelines, patient role, or prevention plan.
